case: Autoload initialization, ordered after the collector autoload
requirement: Same obligations as F040 with reversed autoload order; a difference between the two exposes an order-dependent blind spot

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: driver.gd (project.godot autoload order: CollectorMarker, UserAutoload -- reversed from F040)

notes: Identical fixture scripts to F040, only the [autoload] section order in project.godot is reversed. Confirmed empirically: with CollectorMarker registered first, UserAutoload's _ready() observes collector_active=true, the opposite of F040's result with the same code. This is the direct proof that gd-tools-style _ready()-activated instrumentation's startup coverage depends entirely on autoload registration order, which is a per-project configuration choice, not a property of the collector alone. Whether a given user's project has their state-initializing autoloads before or after wherever gd-tools inserts its own collector autoload determines whether this fixture's F040 or F091 outcome applies to them.
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
ambiguities: Same caveat as F040: this models a _ready()-activated collector. If BP04 finds gd-tools actually activates via a pre-run hook script invoked by the GUT test runner rather than pure autoload order, this ordering experiment needs a companion fixture for that activation path instead of assuming it transfers unchanged.
